company.name: Ferngrove Media
company.one_line: A mobile app where young creators share short cooking videos with their followers.

market.description: Short-form recipe video sharing among Gen Z home cooks, competing for attention against general short-video platforms.

competitors.name: Skillet Social
competitors.positioning: General short-video app with a large but unfocused cooking category
competitors.relative_strength: Ten times the daily active users, but recipes are buried in a mixed feed

competitors.name: Whisk & Co
competitors.positioning: Recipe-first app with structured ingredient lists and grocery integration
competitors.relative_strength: Stronger retention among users who already cook regularly

competitors.name: Tablescape
competitors.positioning: Creator monetization platform for food influencers
competitors.relative_strength: Better creator payouts, pulling top creators away from Ferngrove

situation.prompt: Ferngrove's Discover feed shows new users a mix of trending videos during their first session, but only 11.3% of new signups return on day 2, well below the 19.0% day-2 return rate for users who follow at least three creators in their first session. Should we redesign the first-session flow to push new users toward following creators immediately, or keep the current trending-first feed and improve recommendation quality instead?
situation.tension: Pushing new users to follow creators immediately adds friction before they have seen any content, and an earlier forced-follow experiment on another surface raised first-session drop-off rather than lowering it.
options: Redesign onboarding to prompt following three creators before showing any feed
Keep the trending-first feed and invest in better first-session recommendation ranking
Run a hybrid: show trending content immediately but surface a lightweight follow prompt after the third video
constraints: No net-new headcount for this quarter
Cannot add another onboarding screen without design review sign-off
Must ship before Whisk & Co's grocery-integration launch next quarter
situation.leadership_belief: The exec team believes the drop in day-2 return is a content-discovery problem, not a social-graph problem, and wants ranking improvements prioritized.

supporting_facts: Day-2 return rate for new signups is 11.3%, versus 19.0% for users who follow at least three creators in their first session.
Ferngrove has 41,000 paying subscribers out of roughly 2.4 million monthly active users.
The onboarding flow currently shows a trending-content feed within 8 seconds of signup, with no follow prompt.
Whisk & Co is launching grocery-list integration next quarter, which Ferngrove does not have.
Skillet Social has roughly ten times Ferngrove's daily active users but a lower share of cooking-specific watch time.
Tablescape pays top creators 22% more per thousand views than Ferngrove's creator fund.
An earlier forced-follow experiment on Ferngrove's search surface reduced first-session completion by 6.4 percentage points.
Gross margin is 76.5%, driven mostly by low video-hosting costs relative to subscription revenue.
Monthly churn among paying subscribers is 3.8%.
The design team has one open headcount for Q3, already allocated to a creator-payments project.
